issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute a meal's price, but the provided solution and template code use a differently named static method computeMealCost(Meal). This naming mismatch between the specification (calculateTotalPrice) and the actual code (computeMealCost) is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which method to implement and what the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the solution/template method computeMealCost(Meal) to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (and update any references), or update the problem statement and UML to refer to computeMealCost(Meal). Ensure the chosen method name appears consistently in the template, solution, and problem text/examples.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) requires a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute the cost of a meal, but both the template comments and the provided solution use the name computeMealCost(Meal). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (computing the meal total) creates a mapping burden: students reading the problem/UML will look for calculateTotalPrice, while the starter/example code and solution implement computeMealCost, which can cause confusion and wasted time.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the solution (and any template references) computeMealCost(Meal) -> calculateTotalPrice(Meal) with the exact signature and static modifier required by the problem/UML, and update calls in Main; or update the problem statement/UML to refer to computeMealCost(Meal). Prefer renaming computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice to match the stated requirements (static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal)).
